language.note: Retains letters þ (thorn) and ð (eth) from Old Norse/Old English — not used in Norwegian, Swedish, or Danish, and one of the most linguistically conservative living Germanic languages
language.script: Latin (extended with þ, ð, and other diacritics)

terrainDescription.zh: 火山與冰河地形為主，多數地區近乎無樹，呈現典型苔原與荒地景觀，與其他北歐國家的森林地形明顯不同。
terrainDescription.en: Dominated by volcanic and glacial terrain; most of the country is famously near-treeless, with classic tundra/barren landscapes that stand in sharp contrast to the forested terrain of the other Nordic countries.

plate.color: white background, black text, Icelandic emblem + "IS" on the left
plate.shape: rectangular, EU-standard 520×110mm, format ABC12 (older AB 123 format still valid but no longer issued)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Yellow bollard with a white top edge/reflector

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not strongly documented beyond general Nordic wooden-pole styles — Iceland's low population and sparse road network mean thinner community documentation than its neighbors; treat as lower-confidence

historicalContext.zh: 冰島語屬北日耳曼語族，與挪威語、瑞典語同源，但自古諾斯語以來變化極小，被視為現存北歐語言中最保守／古老的一支，至今保留 þ、ð 等古字母，是辨識度極高的文字特徵；冰島並非維也納道路標誌公約締約國，但標誌設計大致與公約系統一致。
historicalContext.en: Icelandic is North Germanic, sharing roots with Norwegian and Swedish, but has changed remarkably little since Old Norse — often considered the most conservative living Nordic language, still using archaic letters like þ and ð, a highly distinctive script feature. Iceland is not a party to the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals, though its sign design is broadly consistent with the convention's system.
